personality_one_liner: A sharp, responsive, tactical command-center designed for rapid workflow automation and AI task execution.

spacing.rule: Handle spacing correctly dont have extra spaces where its not required, handle padding and margin corectly and subtle for buttons and components

do's: Use solid surfaceSecondary with border for elevated surfaces
dont's: Do not use blur or glass effects (clashes with the sharp, tactical utility aesthetic)

screens.name: Agent
screens.purpose: A chat interface for interacting with the AI agent, displaying inline tool execution cards.

states.loading: Subtle pulse on the input area
states.empty: Empty chat with suggested prompt pills (e.g., 'Run daily report', 'Create webhook workflow')
states.error: Failed tool execution card with red status badge and retry button

screens.layout: Standard chat layout (messages in ScrollView, sticky input at bottom). AI messages are left-aligned, user right-aligned. Crucially, when AI executes a tool (n8n workflow), inject a 'Task Card' (surfaceSecondary block, border, status badge: Running/Completed) into the chat stream.

screens.name: Workflows
screens.purpose: List of all automated workflows with quick active/inactive toggles.

states.empty: Illustration of connected nodes + 'No workflows yet' + CTA to create

screens.layout: Search bar at top. Vertical list of workflow cards. Card layout: Title, Trigger icon, Next run / Last run timestamp, and an active/inactive switch. FAB floating bottom right for 'New Workflow'.

screens.name: WorkflowEditor
screens.purpose: Vertical node chain builder for creating/editing a workflow.

states.empty: Not applicable (always starts with Trigger node)
states.error: Validation error banner at the top of the canvas

screens.layout: Vertical node chain (not 2D canvas). Starts with Trigger block. A vertical line connects down to a '+' icon, then to the next Action block (e.g., HTTP, LLM, Webhook). Tapping a node opens a bottom sheet with its configuration form. Sticky 'Save' button at the bottom.

screens.name: Runs
screens.purpose: Execution history showing success/failure of recent workflow runs.
screens.layout: Command-center style list. Each row shows Workflow Name, Timestamp, and a hard status badge (Success: green, Failed: red). Tapping expands the row to show a console-like log view (surfaceTertiary background, mono text).

screens.name: Settings
screens.purpose: Configure LLM providers, local endpoints, and external n8n instance.

states.error: Validation error on API key inputs

screens.layout: Form-heavy layout. Grouped sections (LLM Provider, n8n Connection). Use segmented controls to toggle between 'Cloud API' (OpenAI/Claude) and 'Local' (Ollama). Clean input fields with borders. Sticky 'Save Configuration' button.

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the Dark-First Utility DARK guidelines. Do not use blue or purple anywhere. Use the defined #FF6B00 (Amber) for primary actions.
For the Workflow Editor, implement a vertical list of nodes connected by a centered vertical line instead of a free-floating 2D canvas. This is crucial for a native mobile experience.
Use Phosphor icons with a consistent weight (either all outlined or all filled per screen context).

Tool execution cards in the Chat Agent must look like distinct tactical blocks (surfaceSecondary, 1px border) with clear status indicators (Running/Success/Failed) so they stand out from normal conversation.
Do not use glassmorphism or blur effects. The app should feel sharp, mechanical, and tactical. Rely on 1px borders (#333333) and surface elevation for separation.
Add firm haptic feedback on node reordering, drag/drop, and workflow execution triggers.
Avoid emoji entirely across the system UI.
